experiment_description: Conditional-X feedback experiment on the IBM Quantum superconducting processor “marrakesh” using a 20-qubit chain. The initial computational-basis state contained six occupied/spin-up qubits localized near the center of the chain. Each circuit iteration consisted of a random scrambling layer followed by a measurement-feedback layer. The scrambling layer used alternating even- and odd-bond nearest-neighbor CZ gates with random single-qubit rotations R^X_j(θ)=exp(-i θ X_j/2); for the main-text experiments the random angles θ were sampled independently from a uniform interval [0,1.0]. After each scrambling layer, qubit x was projectively measured in the computational/Z basis with probability f(x)=g(L-x), with L=20 and g=0.01. If the measured outcome was 0, a conditional Pauli-X gate was applied to that qubit; if the outcome was 1, no flip was applied; unmeasured qubits were left unchanged. The circuit was evolved for 10 layers and averaged over 10 random circuit realizations. The local density was n_x=|0_x><0_x|, and the measured density profile was normalized as N_j(t)=<n_j(t)>/sum_x <n_x(t)>. For continuum fitting, u=j/L is the dimensionless coordinate in [0,1], t is the circuit-layer index, N(u,t) is the normalized density, γ is the coefficient of the position-dependent feedback-loss term, and D is the effective diffusion coefficient in the phenomenological equation ∂_t N(u,t)=-(1-u) γ N(u,t)+D ∂^2_u N(u,t).

conditional_x_feedback_loss_rate_gamma_p.description: Fitted dimensionless coefficient of the position-dependent loss term in the decay-diffusion reconstruction of the measured normalized density profile.

conditional_x_feedback_diffusion_coeffic.description: Fitted effective diffusion coefficient in the decay-diffusion reconstruction of the measured normalized density profile.

experiment_description: Conditional-SWAP feedback experiment on the IBM Quantum superconducting processor “marrakesh” using a 20-qubit chain. The initial computational-basis state contained six occupied/spin-up qubits localized near the center of the chain. Each circuit iteration consisted of the same random scrambling layer used in the main text, built from alternating even- and odd-bond nearest-neighbor CZ gates and random single-qubit R^X rotations with independently sampled angles θ in [0,1.0], followed by a brickwork measurement-feedback layer on nearest-neighbor bonds. In the feedback layer, each bond operation measured the left qubit x in the computational/Z basis with fixed probability p_SWAP=0.3; if the measured outcome was 0, a SWAP gate was applied between qubits x and x+1, while if the outcome was 1 no SWAP was applied; with probability 1-p_SWAP the bond was left unchanged. The circuit was evolved for 10 layers and averaged over 10 random circuit realizations. The local density was n_x=|0_x><0_x|, and the measured density profile was normalized as N_j(t)=<n_j(t)>/sum_x <n_x(t)>. For continuum fitting, u=j/L is the dimensionless coordinate in [0,1], t is the circuit-layer index, N(u,t) is the normalized density, v is the emergent drift velocity, and D2, D3, and D4 are higher-order spatial spreading coefficients in the phenomenological drift-diffusion expansion ∂_t N=-v ∂_u N + D2 ∂^2_u N + D3 ∂^3_u N + D4 ∂^4_u N.

conditional_swap_drift_velocity_dimensio.description: Fitted emergent drift velocity from the higher-order drift-diffusion reconstruction of the measured normalized density profile.

conditional_swap_second_order_spreading_.description: Fitted second-derivative coefficient in the higher-order drift-diffusion reconstruction of the measured normalized density profile.

conditional_swap_third_order_spreading_c.description: Fitted third-derivative coefficient in the higher-order drift-diffusion reconstruction of the measured normalized density profile.

conditional_swap_fourth_order_spreading_.description: Fitted fourth-derivative coefficient in the higher-order drift-diffusion reconstruction of the measured normalized density profile.

experiment_description: Large-scale 100-qubit IBM Quantum “marrakesh” simulation comparing three circuit architectures with the same central initial state. The selected chain had L=100 qubits, initialized with six occupied/spin-up qubits at the center. The random scrambling layer used nearest-neighbor CZ gates in an even/odd brickwork pattern plus random single-qubit R^X rotations with main-text random-angle range [0,1.0]. Three evolutions were run: a purely unitary random circuit; a random circuit with position-dependent mid-circuit computational-basis measurements but no conditional feedback; and a random circuit with the same position-dependent measurements plus conditional X feedback. For the monitored circuits, the measurement probability was f(x)=g(L-x) with g=0.15/L. The conditional-X feedback rule applied a Pauli-X gate to a measured qubit only when the measurement outcome was 0. The circuit depth was swept over layers i=1 through i=10 and the data were averaged over 10 random circuit realizations. The measured local density was n_x=|0_x><0_x|. The reported scalar observable was the net center-of-mass shift δN_c(i)=L[N_c(i)-N_c(1)], where N_c(i)=sum_x x <n_x(i)>/sum_x <n_x(i)> using the paper’s plotted normalized position convention.

final_center_of_mass_shift_conditional_x.description: Approximate net center-of-mass shift at the final measured circuit layer for the conditional-X feedback circuit, read from the plotted IBM hardware data.

final_center_of_mass_shift_pure_mid_circ.description: Approximate net center-of-mass shift at the final measured circuit layer for the random circuit with position-dependent mid-circuit measurements but without conditional feedback, read from the plotted IBM hardware data.

final_center_of_mass_shift_unitary_rando.description: Approximate net center-of-mass shift at the final measured circuit layer for the purely unitary random circuit, read from the plotted IBM hardware data.

The selected chain had L=100 qubits, initialized with six occupied/spin-up qubits localized near the right boundary. The random scrambling layer used nearest-neighbor CZ gates in an even/odd brickwork pattern plus random single-qubit R^X rotations with main-text random-angle range [0,1.0]. Three evolutions were run: a purely unitary random circuit; a random circuit with position-dependent mid-circuit computational-basis measurements but no conditional feedback; and a random circuit with the same position-dependent measurements plus conditional X feedback. The conditional-X feedback rule applied a Pauli-X gate to a measured qubit only when the measurement outcome was 0. The circuit depth was swept over layers i=1 through i=10 and the data were averaged over 10 random circuit realizations. The measured local density was n_x=|0_x><0_x|. The reported scalar observable was the net center-of-mass shift δN_c(i)=L[N_c(i)-N_c(1)], where N_c(i)=sum_x x <n_x(i)>/sum_x <n_x(i)> using the paper’s plotted normalized position convention.

final_right_edge_center_of_mass_shift_pu.description: Approximate net center-of-mass shift at the final measured circuit layer for the random circuit with position-dependent mid-circuit measurements but without conditional feedback and with right-edge initialization, read from the plotted IBM hardware data.

experiment_description: End-to-end polarization measurement of feedback-directed transport on the IBM Quantum “marrakesh” processor. Chains of L=50, 80, and 100 qubits were initialized with six occupied/spin-up qubits at the center. Each circuit layer used the random scrambling architecture made of nearest-neighbor CZ gates in an even/odd brickwork pattern and random single-qubit R^X rotations with main-text random-angle range [0,1.0]. For the feedback runs, each scrambling layer was followed by position-dependent computational-basis mid-circuit measurements with f(x)=g(L-x), where g=0.18/L, and conditional X feedback in which a Pauli-X gate was applied only after measurement outcome 0. The circuit depth was swept over layers i=1 through i=10, and results were averaged over 10 random circuit realizations. The measured local density was n_x=|0_x><0_x|. The transport diagnostic was the end-to-end polarization J_c(i)=[<n_{L-1}(i)>-<n_0(i)>]/sum_x <n_x(i)>, comparing the occupations at the two ends of the chain.

maximum_end_to_end_polarization_conditio.description: Largest end-to-end polarization reported for the conditional-X feedback circuits over the measured large-system data set.
